# BOOK 1 OF 2: Ruth Fielding at Golden Pass (Alice B. Emerson, 1925, Cupples & Leon)

## Characters
- **Ruth Fielding**: heroine, scenario writer/director, Fielding Film Corporation; orphan raised at Red Mill by Uncle Jabez and Aunt Alvirah.
- **Tom Cameron**: Helen's twin, Ruth's business partner, loves Ruth, jealous of Layton Boardman. Brave; rescues Ruth at cliff ledge; shot/clawed by bear.
- **Helen Cameron**: Ruth's chum, engaged to Chess Copley; hit by spent bullet at rodeo (scalp wound).
- **Chess Copley**: Helen's fiancé; uncle's money backs his business deal.
- **Uncle Jabez Potter**: crabby great-uncle. **Aunt Alvirah Boggs**: housekeeper, calls Ruth "my pretty."
- **Jennie Marchand ("Heavy", née Stone)**: married to Henri Marchand (French); in France.
- **Ann Hicks, Nettie Parsons, Mary Cox ("The Fox"), Mercy Curtis**: school chums (Briarwood Hall).
- **Barclay Clayton ("Bark")**: Nettie/Ruth escort.
- **Mr. Hammond**: president, Alectrion Film Corporation; suggests Ruth act; sends for Edith Lang.
- **Layton Boardman**: western actor, hero; from Palatial Films (owner Sol Bloomberg). Injured (ankle, back) when horse throws him. Says he's no lady's man, "drilled" love scenes.
- **Viola Callahan**: temperamental actress (Brennan contract); jumps contract to Bloomberg with lover Tony Martano; note left.
- **Charlie Reid**: Bloomberg's agent, met Viola in Chicago.
- **Sol Bloomberg**: rival owner, enemy of Boardman/Ruth.
- **Edith Lang**: crippled ex-actress (WWI Red Cross, leg amputated), coaches Ruth.
- **Ma and Pa Gowdy**: Headwaters Ranch owners. **Andy**: gangling ranch youth. Foreman: long, lean, blue-eyed.
- **Shepley**: tall thin director, Ruth's right hand. Dave Sentner: comedian. Two cameramen.
- **Anita Townsend and Grand**: co-stars of "Snowblind."

## Plot in order
1. **Ch I**: Cheslow premiere of "Snowblind" at the Palace (Main Street). Chums surprise Ruth with "Sweetbriars" yell. Ruth speaks on stage; explosion, fire, lights out.
2. **Ch II**: Tom rescues Ruth from smoke behind stage. Background of series (Red Mill, Briarwood, Jennie, Ruth's scenario "The Heart of a Schoolgirl").
3. **Ch III**: Crowd outside; Aunt Alvirah reunites. Explosion was films in storeroom; mostly smoke. Party at hotel. Mr. Hammond arrives; Golden Pass, Montana, chosen for "Hearts of the Mountains."
4. **Ch IV**: Mr. Hammond describes Golden Pass. Ruth invites Layton Boardman (telegraphed earlier). Ruth gets Boardman, hero, contract; Tom suspicious. Tom and Helen re Chess's uncle, "snowball property."
5. **Ch V-VII**: Tom objects to Boardman; Bloomberg mention. Viola Callahan hired at high salary; Ruth distrusts her.
6. **Ch VIII**: Party at Red Mill; Boardman dances, charms guests; Tom dances with Ruth to block Boardman. Girls leave next day by train.
7. **Ch IX-X**: Trip to Chicago. Viola boards. Viola meets Charlie Reid (Bloomberg agent) secretly; Ruth and Helen spot it.
8. **Ch XI**: Train to Golden Pass. Arrive at Headwaters Ranch (Ma Gowdy, Pa Gowdy, Andy). Helen shares Ruth's room. Tom goes hunting, quarrel with Ruth.
9. **Ch XII**: Stampede of steers; Ruth trapped. Boardman's horse throws him; Tom and cowboys shoot steers. Boardman's ankle hurt, head bleeding.
10. **Ch XIII-XIV**: Ruth visits Boardman in bed (Tom sees, glum). Rodeo planned. Viola taunts. Rodeo day: Helen struck by spent bullet from cowboy's real cartridge.
11. **Ch XV**: Helen treated by Ruth (Red Cross training). Viola's note: "Sorry, but Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg..."
12. **Ch XVI-XVII**: Mr. Hammond arrives (by car). Proposes Ruth act lead. Tom jealous; walk with Tom ("If I could be sure it was all just play acting!").
13. **Ch XVIII-XIX**: Screen tests, Ruth films well. Hammond suggests Edith Lang as coach; Edith arrives, coaches Ruth. Tom goes to hills, meets bear at water hole.
14. **Ch XX**: Tom and bear on rock; Ruth arrives; bear leaves ("I'm a cowgirl, Tom!").
15. **Ch XXI-XXII**: Avalanche planned (cabins, cave). Ruth slips off ledge; Tom catches, climbs down to ledge, grabs sapling; Ruth drops into his arms; Boardman returns with lariat to rescue. Avalanche day: Ruth in cave; second unplanned explosion (dynamite house) buries cave.
16. **Ch XXIII-XXIV**: Buried alive. Tom finds tunnel and daylight. Two bears in second cave; Tom shoots one (ex: "Got him!" from Boardman); Tom's arm raked. Ruth tourniquet with twig. Tom recovers.
17. **Ch XXV**: Chess arrives, business good, marriage soon. Boardman tells Tom he never cared for girls ("drilled" love). Tom grins. Film premieres in New York as "Hearts of the Mountains." Ruth lifted onstage. Bloomberg's film with Viola fails; Viola's chances hurt. Helen envious: "With the world at your feet, to say nothing of Tom!" THE END.

## Key details
- Ruth's picture: "Snowblind" (first hit); "Hearts of the Mountains" (second, Golden Pass).
- Lines: Sweetbriars yell ("S.B.—Ah-h-h!", "Briarwood Hall!").
- Viola note text: "Sorry, but Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg..."
- Hotel in Cheslow; Chicago hotel; Headwaters Ranch; Golden Pass station; ledge; cave.
- Rodeo: bronco busting, steer roping, bull throwing.

# BOOK 2 OF 2: The Case of the Black Twenty-Two (Brian Flynn, 1929, Macrae Smith / Grosset & Dunlap)

## Characters
- **Peter Daventry**: junior partner, "Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry, Solicitors," Cornhill, London; Oxford man; narrator-companion.
- **David Linnell**: senior partner, Lancashire-born, 58.
- **Plunkett**: elderly clerk, 35 years service. **Collins**: office messenger.
- **Laurence P. Stewart**: American millionaire, collector of Mary Queen of Scots relics; Assynton Lodge, Berkshire; murdered in library.
- **Charles Stewart**: his son, ~22; engaged to Rosemary Armitage ("The Towers").
- **Marjorie Lennox**: ward, "M. L."; lace handkerchief; petite, retroussé nose, blue eyes.
- **Morgan Llewellyn**: secretary, ~early 30s, pince-nez, reddish-brown eyes; wrote love letter to Marjorie.
- **John Butterworth**: butler, 60+, ex-Sir Julian Kennedy's butler; murderer of Stewart; daughter Alice Mortimer.
- **Mrs. Butterworth**: housekeeper.
- **Colonel Leach-Fletcher**: neighbor, "Neuve Chapelle" bungalow; dined at Assynton that night; Bentley car.
- **Detective-Inspector Goodall**: Scotland Yard; stout, clean-shaven, blue serge.
- **Sergeant Clegg**: local Berkshire sergeant; "By Gum!"
- **P.C. Potter**: constable.
- **Anthony Bathurst**: amateur investigator; Uppingham, Oxford; brother-of-friend Gerald Daventry's acquaintance.
- **Gerald Daventry**: Peter's brother, accountant.
- **Day, Forshaw and Palmers**: auctioneers, Hanover Galleries. **Ronald Forshaw**: young man. **Mr. Day**: partner.
- **Jim Mason**: night-watchman murdered (skull). **Edward Druce**: other watchman, ~60, daughter Poppy.
- **Mrs. Turner**: cleaner.
- **Michael O'Connor**: giant foundryman, black beard. **Patrick O'Connor**: boot-boy, 18, bicycle.
- **Maidment**: gardener.
- **Blanchard**: Blanchard's Hotel, Clifford Street; **Atkins**: porter; **Rabjohns**: chambermaid.
- **Ferguson (Andrew)**: Crake and Ferguson, NY solicitors.
- **Waring**: Goodall's assistant.
- **Marriott**: Peter's friend at lunch.
- **Snoop Mortimer ("Flash Alf")**: NY crook, posing as Laurence C. Stewart; wife Alice (Butterworth's daughter), hay fever.

## Plot in order
1. **Ch I**: Peter hungover at Cornhill office. Linnell: Laurence P. Stewart's letter (dated June 7) commissions purchase at Day, Forshaw & Palmers sale (June 10) of Lots 37 Pearl Collar, 38 Antique Tapestry Fire-screen, 39 Rosary of Amber Beads, "property of Mary, Queen of Scots." Peter lunches at Violette (Gustave waiter); man and woman at next table; Peter says "Queen Anne's dead!" / "So's Mary, Queen of Scots!"; man knocks cruet to floor.
2. **Ch II**: Peter views items at Hanover Galleries; two plainclothes men watch. Screen beads spell "JESUS CHRIST, GOD AND SAVIOUR"; corners: Scots Lion, fleur-de-lis, Leopards and Lilies. Linnell suspects fraud; telegrams from "Stewart": "Say what the hell's biting you..." Next day Linnell goes; murder discovered.
3. **Ch III**: Hanover Galleries murder: Mason dead, items stolen. Druce's evidence: woman asked directions to Marble Arch, Mason distracted. Forshaw: Peter asked how many viewed items. Phone call: Stewart murdered at Assynton.
4. **Ch IV**: Goodall questions. Peter/Linnell; Peter to Leyton cricket, then Gerald finds Bathurst at Princes Club (squash). Peter recruits Bathurst.
5. **Ch V**: Sergeant Clegg at Assynton library: Stewart at desk, skull smashed, revolver in left dressing-gown pocket, one shot fired; door locked inside, French doors bolted. Note: "Urgent in the morning! M. L." Clegg finds lace handkerchief initialed M. L. behind curtain.
5b. **Ch VI**: Marjorie interview; accuses Llewellyn; denies being in library; sobs.
6. **Ch VII**: Butterworth: last saw Stewart 10 p.m.; heard voices ~10:10, one a woman's (Marjorie's). Maid Barton, Regan, Evans, Winter; cook Mrs. Briggs; gardener Maidment; boot-boy O'Connor.
7. **Ch VIII**: Train 6:55 from Paddington: Goodall boards with Peter and Bathurst. Bathurst: "a compliment is a tribute to ability." Peter tells lunch story.
8. **Ch IX**: Assynton station; Goodall meets Clegg. Night at Assynton Lodge; Charles's room. Bathurst hears prowler ~1:22 a.m.; next morning Llewellyn introduced.
9. **Ch X**: Bathurst at foundry; Michael O'Connor reveals Patrick's bicycle had tar on tyres (road under tarmac work), used night of murder. Bathurst examines bicycle; only one in shed.
10. **Ch XI**: Library reconstruction. Ink-bowl mud; stones in coal-scuttle; Bathurst's circle (center Hanover Galleries, radius a mile) to find hotel. Goodall sends Clegg.
11. **Ch XII**: Museum Room catalogue (2,044 items). Llewellyn describes screen (metal, Mary's Lion). Second screen missing (No. 866 in catalogue). Marjorie describes screen: "Timeo Danaos," fish in center, Leopards/Lilies. Trunk call to Blanchard's, Regent 9999; "Mr. and Mrs. Laurence Charles Stewart" from New York; left at once.
12. **Ch XIII**: Colonel Leach-Fletcher at "Neuve Chapelle": Stewart worried about treachery, papers tampered with; son's conduct; interview planned that night. Colonel saw Renan's Vie de Jésus open on desk.
13. **Ch XIV**: Bathurst deduces Llewellyn: love letter found in Renan book (to Marjorie, threatening). Stone path piece found in pool (Peter wades). Bullet-weapon theory; Peter fires shots to test.
14. **Ch XV-XVI**: Bullet found embedded in *Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure* (848 pages). Bathurst reconstructs: light switch, Stewart fired in dark.
15. **Ch XVII**: Memoir passage about "the Black Twenty-Two," Girardier made two screens; Cardinal of Lorraine's gift.
16. **Ch XVIII**: Bathurst at Blanchard's; Blanchard, Atkins (wife read clock, black glasses), Rabjohns (odor of burning, asthma remedy). Room 54.
17. **Ch XIX**: Supper at Ricardo's Soho with Goodall; Bathurst reveals bullet and stone.
18. **Ch XX**: British Museum; Times/Telegraph personal "M. S. Ring Regent 9999 ... Both well!" = Mary Stewart / Bothwell. Peter phones; Bathurst's flat (Emily).
19. **Ch XXI**: Ferguson of New York arrives; will: Butterworth £500 p.a., Llewellyn £300, Marjorie £250,000 if marries Charles (forfeited if marries other), residue to Charles.
20. **Ch XXII**: Bathurst-Charles talk; Charles loves Rosemary Armitage; father threatened him; Bathurst orders house closed.
21. **Ch XXIII**: Night stakeout; Colonel's Bentley; Goodall arrests "Snoop" Mortimer and Alice Mortimer and Butterworth.
22. **Ch XXIV-XXV**: Screen fish swings; cavity holds 22 black pearls ("Twenty-Two Black Pearls of Lorraine"). ICHTHUS solution: Greek letters of "Jesus Christ God Saviour" initials = Fish. Bathurst reveals reasoning. Charles: Marjorie's will share offsets; wedding gift idea. Ends.

## Key details
- Dates: letter June 7; sale June 10; Mason murder night June 8/9 (Hanover); Stewart killed night June 8 (~11 p.m.).
- Prices: none stated for pearls.
- Druce's "sneezing" clue; woman in dark clothes, age 30-40.
- Bathurst's rules: "M. L." = Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry.
